document.title: Locality-Preserving Hashing for Shifts with Connections to Cryptography

candidate.title: An Optimal Two-Dimensional Locality-Preserving Hash for Shifts
candidate.subtitle: The source's Random-Walk-Hash achieves the error rate its own lower bound allows
candidate.one_line: The Random-Walk-Hash algorithm printed in the source is a 2-dimensional (d, delta)-LPHS with delta = O~(1/d), matching the source's own Omega(1/d) lower bound.
candidate.informal: Two parties each hold a huge random two-dimensional array, one being the other shifted by one step along some axis. Neither may read more than d entries, they cannot communicate, and each must output a position so that the two positions differ by exactly the shift. In one dimension the optimal error is known to be about 1/d^2; in two dimensions the source proves no scheme beats 1/d, gives one achieving d^{-7/8}, and prints a different symmetric algorithm -- a sequence of deterministic random walks with geometrically growing step sizes -- whose error its experiments put at 1/d. It could not prove that, and this conjecture is that the printed algorithm really does achieve it.
candidate.status_note: Open, and asserted rather than asked: the source prints the algorithm, conjectures the error rate, reports experiments consistent with it, states that it could not analyse it, and leaves settling it to future work. A proof would close the two-dimensional case, since the matching lower bound is the source's own Theorem 1.4.
candidate.progress_note: The source gives the full heuristic analysis and reduces it to two unproved facts about meeting times of random walks on Z^2, plus an independence assumption that the algorithm's loop-breaking rule violates. Its experiments agree with the conjectured rate; the paper does not report their scale.

candidate.why_interesting: The lower bound is already proved, so this single statement is the whole remaining gap in the two-dimensional case, and the algorithm is printed and implementable. It also carries directly to the distributed discrete logarithm problem, which is the bottleneck in group-based homomorphic secret sharing, through the source's own two-way reduction.
candidate.why_clean: The algorithm is three short procedures, the error notion is one probability, and the conjecture is a single upper bound with a matching known lower bound.
candidate.risks: The conjecture is about a specific printed algorithm, not about the existence of some O~(1/d) scheme, and the page states the former; check that the transcription of Algorithms 1, 7 and 8 is exact, in particular the last step size, which is sqrt(d'/2) and not sqrt(d')/2 -- the PDF text layer flattens the radical. The hypotheses on n and b are left as 'large enough' because the source's statement of the conjecture names none.
candidate.formal_statement_latex: There is a function $c(\cdot)$, polylogarithmic in its argument, such that for all large enough $n$ and $b$, the algorithm Random-Walk-Hash$(\cdot, d)$ is a 2-dimensional $(d, \delta)$-LPHS with $\delta \le c(d)/d$.

verify.reason: The conjecture is printed under the heading 'Conjectured optimal algorithm' in Section 4.1.4, restated in the introduction, and explicitly left open; nothing later in the paper analyses the algorithm. Two corrections were forced: the last step size was first transcribed as sqrt(d')/2 from the text layer, which is wrong, and the hypotheses on n and b were first invented rather than left open as the source leaves them.

checks.name: existence
checks.finding: Section 4.1.4, PDF p. 24: 'We conjecture that the following symmetric algorithm (Random-Walk-Hash) has the optimal performance of delta = O~(1/d).' Restated on PDF p. 7.

checks.name: openness
checks.finding: 'However, we were not able to rigorously analyze it', and on PDF p. 7 'settling our conjecture is left open for future work'. Section 4.2 proves the lower bound, not this upper bound; no later section returns to the algorithm.

checks.name: strength
checks.finding: Stated about the printed algorithm, as the source states it, rather than as the weaker existence claim. The weaker reading is named on the page and explicitly not adopted.

checks.name: quantifiers-and-parameters
checks.finding: The source's conjecture names no hypothesis on n or b, while neighbouring lemmas assume n = Omega(d) and 2^b >= d^4 or b >= 3 log n. The statement says 'for all large enough n and b' and flags this; a reviewer should pin it down.

checks.name: attribution
checks.finding: The source's own conjecture about its own algorithm. The one-dimensional optimum it builds on is attributed to Dinur-Keller-Klein, as the source attributes it.

checks.name: definitions
checks.finding: The final step size is sqrt(d'/2), with the radical over d'/2, confirmed by rendering PDF p. 25 at 150 dpi; the text layer flattens it and reads as sqrt(d')/2. The first draft had the wrong one. Also corrected: the per-stage failure exponent, which is d'^{-2^{-l}} counting Min-Hash as the first stage, not d'^{-2^{-(l+1)}}.

checks.name: fabrication
checks.finding: The two random-walk claims and the loop-breaking obstruction are the source's own, quoted or closely paraphrased. The step-size pattern d'^{1/2-2^{-(l+1)}} is this page's arithmetic on the printed exponents 1/4, 3/8, 7/16 and is labelled as a description of them.

checks.name: self-containment
checks.finding: All three procedures and the LPHS definition are printed on the page; a reader needs nothing from the source to attempt it.

corrections.problem: Last step size transcribed from the text layer as sqrt(d')/2.
corrections.corrected: sqrt(d'/2), read off the rendered page.

corrections.problem: Per-stage failure probability exponent was off by one in the setting prose.
corrections.corrected: d'^{-2^{-l}} with Min-Hash counted as the first stage, consistent with the source's O(d'^{-1/4}), O(d'^{-1/8}) for the first two rw-stages.

corrections.problem: First draft invented hypotheses n = Omega(d) and 2^b >= d^4.
corrections.corrected: Leave them as 'large enough' and record in a remark that the source's own statement names none.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Obtaining optimal parameters for k-dimensional LPHS for general k -- the source's 'main question, on which we make partial progress' (PDF p. 8).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: A programme rather than a proposition: no value is conjectured for general k, and the source's lower bound Omega(d^{-2/k}) is not claimed to be optimal. The k = 2 case is the one the source commits to, and that is c/0062.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Whether LPHS-based sketches provide an optimal tradeoff between sketch size and error probability (PDF p. 8).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: Posed as a question with no committed answer and no account of what blocks it; the source says only that a negative result from [23] rules out non-adaptive sublinear-time LPHS and 'in fact holds even for sketching'.

rejected_in_this_paper.what: Designing a 2-dimensional LPHS that makes monotone queries along one axis, which would avoid loops and be much easier to analyse (PDF p. 24).
rejected_in_this_paper.why: A design goal the source explicitly does not know how to meet -- 'we do not know how to design such an algorithm with similar performance' -- with no claim that it is possible. Recorded as part of the obstruction on c/0062.
